description.narrative:
Boreholes remain the backbone of rural and peri-urban water supply systems across Somaliland, serving as critical lifelines for communities dependent on groundwater. However, these assets are increasingly vulnerable to seasonal floods, surface contamination, and gradual deterioration due to lack of adequate protection. Thisproposal outlines a practical, cost-effective, and sustainable intervention to construct reinforced concrete protective structures around ten strategic boreholes across three regionsof Somaliland.
The project, with a total budget of USD 12,000, seeks to safeguard water quality,ensure uninterrupted access, and strengthen resilience of community water infrastructure. By protecting these boreholes, the Ministry will mitigate risks of contamination and damage, extend their operational lifespan, and enhance public health outcomes for thousands of residents.
Project Objectives  To construct reinforced concrete protective structures around ten boreholes in three regions of Somaliland.  To minimize risks of contamination andflood-related damage.  To ensure long-term sustainability and reliability of water supply for communities.  To improve resilienceof community water infrastructure in line with MoWRD’s water security strategy.
Sustainability The proposed structures are designed to be low-maintenance and highly durable. Sustainability will be reinforced through:  Community water committees responsible for routine monitoring.  Integration into MoWRD’s national water infrastructure maintenance framework.  Use of locally available materials and labor, enhancing ownership and local capacity.
This project presents a timely and strategic intervention to safeguard Somaliland’s most vital water infrastructure. By constructing protective structures around ten boreholes, MoWRD will strengthen water security, improve community health, and enhance resilience to climate variability. The proposed budget is modest compared to the long-term social and economic benefits.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.
